recipes.name: Easy Chicken Tetrazzini
ingredients_raw: 2 (10.75 ounce) cans condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Put cooked spaghetti noodles into 9x13-inch baking dish. Place chicken on top of spaghetti.

Bring condensed soup, water, butter, and bouillon to a boil in a medium saucepan. Pour soup mixture over pasta and chicken and mix to coat pasta withe sauce. Sprinkle Cheddar on top and press down a bit.
Bake uncovered in the preheated oven until bubbly and cheese is melted, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Chicken Tetrazzini
raw_recipe.description: Chicken tetrazzini is an easy meal the whole family will love — just layer cooked noodles and chicken with a creamy soup-based sauce and lots of cheese.

review.reviewBody: My new favorite!!! I used a whole fryer, reserving ALL of the broth and straining it. Many other reviewers said to add 1 cream of chicken and 1 cream of mushroom soup, and that's what I did. I also used chicken broth instead of water for the saucepan mixture. I also added 1/4 tsp. garlic powder and 1/4 tsp onion powder, and I salted and peppered to taste as well. I boiled Angel Hair pasta 16 oz. in the remaining chicken broth, It made ALL the difference in the world! I used a Kroger brand cheese, they have a wonderful medium sharp cheddar, yum! To top off the cheese I sprinkled a little Progresso Italian style bread crumbs over all(another reviewersuggestion). I think you could lay some broccoli, or some other green on top of pasta and pour chicken mixture on top of that and have a one dish meal. I also think I remember that from another reviewer, thanks. The recipe I had was SO bland, but not this one, full of flavor! Oh, and I did put in mushrooms and it was wonderful!!! Thanks so much for the new addition to my recipe box. I am not a creative cook that throws in a pinch of this and a little of that, I cook strictly from recipies 80% of the time, so these reviews from everyone really help me. Thank you to EVERYONE!!!

After reading the reviews I realized what a great base recipe Marion has provided. You add or delete to your personal preference. I like to cut my chicken breast into cubes while frozen since it's easier to cut and it makes less mess and let them thaw in fridge. I added lemon pepper, garlic powder, a little salt and fresh ground black pepper to ziplock bag with chicken and tossed to coat. I used one tbsp of butter and 2 tbsp of olive oil and sauteed chicken till just about cooked through. In place of the bouillon and water I also used low sodium chicken broth. I used 1 can of cream of mushroom and 1 can of cream of chicken 99% fat free since I only had one can of each on hand. I also diced up a small onion and added one can of mushrooms. This turned out really good so thanks again Marion for a recipe that can be tweaked to everyones preference.

Very good and wow! It makes alot (as others have warned)! I used fettucini noodles (broken in half) b/c I'm all out of spaghetti and the first thing I thought this dish needed was a little color from some veggies. When melting the butter (B4 adding the soups), I added some fresh/sliced mushrooms, some chopped celery, minced onion, and some chopped green bell pepper. I sauted them for a few min until soft and then added the soup. Also, I used 2c water and added 1/4c white wine. Finally, when mixing it all together, I added a jar of diced pimentos and a little more sharp cheddar cheese. Very basic recipe that allows you to easily add/subtract and the result was very tasty! Thanks Marian!

Great quick and flavorful recipe! I did alter a bit. We only had gluten free penne pasta so i used that. While cooking the chicken the last couple of minutes, I added 1/2 cup of chopped onion, some fresh spinach and about a 1/2 cup of chopped mushrooms. Then seasoned with minced garlic and pepper.

 For the sauce...we didn't have cream of chicken, but had cream of mushroom soup. In addition, I used about 2 tablespoons of Italian seasoning, garlic, and black pepper.

 Finally I sprinkled with cheddar cheese as directed, but also added grated parmesan cheese, parsley , and seasoned breadcrumbs for added texture. I cooked at 350 covered with foil for 15 min. Then cooked for 10 minutes with foil off. 

My husband only left the decoration on the plate! Delicious!!

I've used this recipe several times as a base. I saute my chicken (I cut it up first) with onions and mushrooms in just a little olive oil and season it with Tony Chachere's creole seasoning, salt, and pepper. *If I don't want the spice I skip the Tony's and opt for garlic powder and salt* I also add a half cup of milk to the cream of chicken mix because it dries out to quickly after removing it from the oven. This is a highly requested meal in my house!

Mostly I make a turkey version of this recipe. I do make my own turkey stock and I do a cheese sauce that I make with cheddar and American cheese and a little heavy cream. When it's about 3/4 done, I top it with busted up ruffled potato chips and turn heat up to 400 degrees farenheit. Let the chips and cheese sauce brown on top and it's done. Sprinkle some chives and cilantro over the top and serve. Looks amazing in Pyrex baking dish

This was a great recipe for me, I had all the ingredients and it was quick. I cubed the chicken and browned it in the butter with garlic powder, onion powder and salt. Then I used penne instead, did not want to go to the grocery store! I mixed all the ingredients including the cheese in a bowl amputee them combined into the baking dish. Lastly I sprinkled some Parmesan cheese and put it in the oven. The top was crispy and my family like it. Next time I will probably add some veggies, like asparagus or brócoli. Thank se,

I cook the chicken with garlic powder and Italian seasoning, use one can of cream of chicken with herbs, one can of cream of chicken and mushroom by Campbell's, and add a can of drained mushrooms. I also find that 1/4 of a cup of cheese isn't enough, so I use a whole small bag of mixed sharp and mild chedder (the kind you can buy for $2 to $3).I also find it's best to get the chicken to just barely cooked before baking so it doesn't dry out during the bake time.

This is good but I make a few changes for my taste. I use egg noodles, 2 cans of cream of mushroom soup, plus a can of mushroom pieces fried for texture, and i use milk not water. My friend gave me a recipe for this but we both lost our copy and this was the closest I've found.

This recipe was super easy. I subbed a can of cream of mushroom soup for one can of cream of chicken. (I just had one, but it worked out well.) I also added ground chicken because I was using the remnants of chicken from the night before. (Also my husband thought the ground chicken looked interesting in the store, so I had that on hand.) The roasted chicken was the better part but ground chicken helped stretch the meat distribution. I added freshly chopped onions, garlic and celery with fresh ground black pepper. I boiled angel hair pasta in low sodium chicken broth instead of using bouillon. I used broth instead of water. I added seasoning salt to dish. But if you are looking for a low sodium dish, maybe you would not need. This recipe serves more than 8 servings. I have a GREEDY family of five and everyone were stuffed with enough for everyone to have a serving the next day, I guess. But upon waking, I learned that the crowd had either finished it off or brought it to work for lunch. ::::Empty casserole::::

It looked like a dish on the cover of a magazine. I was going to take a picture but the crowd had already started digging in.

I made this for a crowd of 20 and it was a hit! I followed the recipe and adjusted it according to the reviews. I sautéed the chicken in butter and added chicken stock, celery, onion, garlic, sweet red peppers as some suggested. After it was cooked, I drained the chicken and discarded the vegetables. The chicken was tender and flavorful. In making the soup base, I used half cream of mushroom and half cream of chicken soups like most reviewers suggested. I also added onion salt, minced garlic, a little cayenne pepper, chicken broth, and white cooking wine (in place of water)to the soup mixture. When I added the cheddar cheese, I mixed it in like several suggested and topped the dish with some additional cheddar cheese, parmesan cheese and butter pats. 
The results were wonderful--very tasty. Several asked for the recipe. If I make this for just my family, I would add broccoli or another green vegetable. I'll definitely make this again. Great for a carry in dinner.
I would use a can of cheddar cheese soup.

My husband's favorite meal is Chicken Tetrazzini. I always use his mom's recipe, but this time I wanted something simpler. This recipe was not only delicious, it was so easy to make. Very happy with it!

I made my own broth with celery, carrots, onions and garlic salt, then used that broth to cook the spaghetti. I also used 1 can cream of mushroom soup with 1 can cream of chicken. I added frozen peas to the layers and used thin spaghetti. Wonderful. Makes about 10 servings.
Easy to make. I added cooked broccoli on top of the chicken and put french fried onions on top of the cheese. Yum! You could use frozen broccoli too.
Next time I will add some Italian seasoning to spice it up a little. Very delicious!

Very easy to prep. I sautéed the chicken, shredded it and added to the sauce. Also added in 8 oz of cream cheese & an extra 1/4 cup of cheddar in the sauce. Mixed the sauce, chicken and pasta before putting it in the baking dish. Will make this again.

I cut this down to make 4 servings and used 1 can of soup. This was husband approved. The flavor is Campbell's chicken noodle soup. I'd prefer much more seasoning. This would be kid friendly. I'd break the noodles in half next time as it would be easier to plate and eat. While I would not eat this again as I am not a fan of chicken noodle soup, my husband really enjoyed it and is looking forward to the leftovers.

I substituted the shredded 5 chicken breasts for a container of the shredded rotisserie chicken from Aldi. It’s seasoned and is just the right amount for this recipe and the seasoning pairs well with the soup and cheese. Love this recipe!
I made a half recipe for the two of us. My husband said he could eat the whole pan. It was very good!
